feedback.problem:
Find, in ascending powers of $k,$ the **first three terms** of the binomial expansion of ${(1-\frac{k}{5})}^{8}.$

${(1-\frac{k}{5})}^{8}=$
{{field-1}}$\,+\,⋯$
feedback.worked_solution:
The first three terms of the binomial expansion for $(1+x)^{n}$ are given by

$$
{(1+x)}^{n}=1+nx+\frac{n(n-1)}{2!}{x}^{2}+⋯.
$$

By substituting $x=-\frac{k}{5}$ and $n=8$ into the above formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1-\frac{k}{5})}^{8} & =1+8\cdot (-\frac{k}{5})+\frac{8(8-1)}{2!}\cdot {(-\frac{k}{5})}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1-\frac{8k}{5}+\frac{8\cdot 7}{2}\cdot \frac{{k}^{2}}{25}+⋯ \\  & =1-\frac{8k}{5}+28\cdot \frac{{k}^{2}}{25}+⋯ \\  & =1-\frac{8}{5}k+\frac{28}{25}{k}^{2}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$
